We aimed to keep the map structure and appearance as close to the original as possible, with over a hundred changes being completely invisible such as adjustments to player clips and blockbullet brushes.

The primary goal of these changes was to improve collision on steps, slopes, doorways, ceilings, and props especially in areas where splash bugs commonly occurred.

Notable examples include smoother movement on top of the crates at mid, improved collision on the concrete ledges leading up to the grass area, and doorway adjustments to prevent players from getting stuck. Additionally, the geometry of the last point has been refined to better match the visuals: for instance, the pipes now only collide with stickies and grenades, which should help facilitate rocket jumping.
The original map, cp_process, was made by Ian "ScorpioUprising" Cuslidge.

Steel is a classic Highlander map beloved by many, but it is not without its flaws.
Released in 2008, Steel shows its age with unclipped stairs, cluttered props, and narrow, chokey corridors.

In this edit of Metalworks, we aimed to stay as close to the vanilla version as possible, while making hundreds of small adjustments to clipping and prop placement.
Our main goal was to fix much of the loose decoration around the map that players commonly use for cover or movement. We addressed this by adding blockbullet brushes to those stacks or replacing them with brush-based structures.
Finally, the geometry of the last point has been improved to better match the visuals. In the original Metalworks, players often struggled with combat due to props forming unstable ramps. In Refresh, we replaced these with clean brush ramps to allow smoother and more consistent fights.
The original map cp_metalworks was made by Ian "ScorpioUprising" Cuslidge.

Upward is often the first map that comes to mind when players think of the Payload gamemode.
As a staple of both competitive and casual play, it is beloved by many, but it is not without its flaws.
Originally released in 2010, Upward has not aged well, suffering from clipping issues, unconventional mapping techniques, and numerous holes.
Refresh has addressed all of these problems while preserving the map that so many players know and love.

Lakeside is an old-school Highlander map originally released in 2010.

In this project, we focused on fixing geometry problems, making minor aesthetic and performance improvements, and adjusting parts of the layout to better suit modern TF2 gameplay.
